headline: International growth lifts sales, margins, and profit
summary_short: Monster Beverage's Q2 2026 net sales rose 20.2% y/y to $2.54B, with net income up 19.6% to $584.5M and diluted EPS up 19.0% to $0.59, while the company repurchased no shares during the quarter.
summary_long: Net sales grew 20.2% y/y (17.9% FX-neutral) to $2.54B, led by the Monster Energy Drinks segment (+21.6%) and international sales (+34.6% y/y, now 46% of total). Gross margin expanded 20bp y/y to 55.9% on pricing and mix, partly offset by higher aluminum-can and freight costs. Operating income rose 17.2% y/y to $740M; net income rose 19.6% to $584.5M and diluted EPS rose 19.0% to $0.59 (adjusted EPS +15.2% to $0.60). No shares were repurchased this quarter, leaving ~$900M authorized. Cash plus short-term investments grew to $3.42B from $2.07B a year ago. The board's previously announced 2-for-1 stock split takes effect August 10-11, 2026. No numeric forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: CEO Hilton Schlosberg cited a strong quarter with net sales +20.2%, diluted EPS +19.0%, and international sales growing to about 46% of total net sales; cited category growth, new consumer attraction, and increased marketing investment across new platforms.

Driven by the Monster Energy Drinks segment (+21.6% y/y) and international sales (+34.6% y/y, now 46% of total); Strategic Brands rose 10.6%, while Alcohol Brands fell 15.2% and the Other segment fell 15.3%.

Margin expansion to 55.9% from 55.7% was attributed to pricing actions and favorable product sales mix, partly offset by higher aluminum can costs, geographic sales mix, and increased freight-in costs.
Higher net sales and gross margin drove the gain, partly offset by higher selling expenses (marketing, sponsorships) and G&A; the effective tax rate also eased to 23.9% from 24.4%.
EPS growth (+19.0%) trailed net income growth (+19.6%) because diluted share count rose slightly y/y (988.5M vs 984.0M) with no buybacks this quarter to offset dilution.
